{% include cheatsheet-header.html %}

> Zeek turns packets into typed, joinable logs. Every connection gets a `uid`, every file a `fuid`, and (with the `community-id` policy loaded) a `community_id` that matches Suricata, EDR and cloud flow logs. Join on those, not on IPs and timestamps. Methods for the timing analysis below are in the [C2 beaconing playbook]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/playbooks/c2-beaconing/).

## Zeek logs that matter

| Log | Key fields | Hunting use |
|---|---|---|
| `conn.log` | `uid`, `id.orig_h/p`, `id.resp_h/p`, `proto`, `service`, `duration`, `orig_bytes`, `resp_bytes`, `conn_state`, `history`, `orig_pkts`, `resp_pkts`, `local_orig`, `community_id` | Beaconing, scanning, exfil volume, long sessions, first-seen pairs; the spine every other log joins to |
| `dns.log` | `query`, `qtype_name`, `rcode_name`, `answers`, `TTLs`, `rejected`, `rtt`, `trans_id` | Tunnelling, DGA, rare domains, resolver bypass, sinkhole answers |
| `http.log` | `method`, `host`, `uri`, `user_agent`, `status_code`, `request_body_len`, `response_body_len`, `resp_mime_types`, `orig_fuids`/`resp_fuids`, `proxied`, `referrer` | Rare user agents, downloads, C2 over HTTP, web shells (POSTs to a static file), long URIs |
| `ssl.log` | `server_name` (SNI), `version`, `cipher`, `established`, `ssl_history` (6.0+), `cert_chain_fps`, `sni_matches_cert` (6.0+), `validation_status`, `ja3`/`ja4` with packages | C2 over TLS, self-signed or mismatched certs, rare client fingerprints, DoH |
| `x509.log` | `fingerprint` (6.0+), `certificate.subject`, `certificate.issuer`, `certificate.not_valid_before/after`, `san.dns`, `certificate.key_length` | Certificate pivots: young certs, default subjects (`CN=localhost`), reused keys |
| `files.log` | `fuid`, `uid`, `id.orig_h`, `id.resp_h`, `source`, `mime_type`, `filename`, `md5`/`sha1`/`sha256` (with `hash-all-files`), `extracted`, `total_bytes` | Payload delivery, exfil of archives, executables over unusual protocols |
| `notice.log` | `note` (`Scan::Address_Scan`, `SSL::Invalid_Server_Cert`, `SSH::Password_Guessing`, `Signatures::Sensitive_Signature`), `msg`, `sub`, `actions` | Leads from Zeek's own detections and loaded packages |
| `weird.log` | `name` (`bad_TCP_checksum`, `data_before_established`, `DNS_RR_unknown_type`, `unknown_protocol`), `addl` | Protocol anomalies: tunnelling, evasion, broken implants |
| `smb_files.log` | `action` (`SMB::FILE_OPEN/WRITE/DELETE/RENAME`), `path`, `name`, `size` | Lateral movement payload drops, ransomware mass writes, staging on shares |
| `smb_mapping.log` | `path` (`\\host\ADMIN$`, `C$`, `IPC$`), `share_type`, `service` | Admin share use, share fan-out from one host |
| `kerberos.log` | `request_type` (AS/TGS), `client`, `service`, `success`, `error_msg`, `cipher`, `forwardable`, `renewable`, `till` | Kerberoasting (RC4 TGS), AS-REP roasting, ticket lifetime oddities, pre-auth failures as a spray signal |
| `ntlm.log` | `username`, `hostname`, `domainname`, `server_nb_computer_name`, `server_dns_computer_name`, `success` | Pass-the-hash, relay (client host name does not match source IP), NTLM where Kerberos is expected |
| `dce_rpc.log` | `endpoint`, `operation`, `rtt`, `named_pipe` | DCSync (`drsuapi` `DRSGetNCChanges`), remote service (`svcctl` `CreateServiceW`), tasks (`atsvc`, `ITaskSchedulerService`), share enum (`srvsvc` `NetrShareEnum`), `samr`/`lsarpc` recon |
| `rdp.log` | `cookie` (client username), `result`, `security_protocol`, `client_name`, `client_build`, `cert_type` | RDP from workstations to workstations, new client names, NLA disabled |
| `ssh.log` | `direction` (INBOUND/OUTBOUND), `auth_success`, `auth_attempts`, `client`, `server`, `host_key`, `hassh`/`hasshServer` with the package | Brute force, outbound SSH from servers, unusual client software, tunnels |
| `ftp.log`, `smtp.log` | `user`, `command`, `arg`, `file_size`; `mailfrom`, `rcptto`, `subject`, `fuids`, `tls` | Legacy exfil; phishing delivery and forwarding |
| `dhcp.log`, `software.log`, `known_services.log`, `known_hosts.log` | `assigned_addr`, `host_name`, `client_fqdn`; `software_type`, `unparsed_version`; `port_num`, `service` | Asset context: who had the IP, what runs where, a new listening service on an old host |
| `ldap.log`, `ldap_search.log` (6.1+) | `operation`, `object`, `filter`, `scope`, `attributes`, `result` | AD recon from the wire (`(servicePrincipalName=*)`, `(objectClass=*)` with subtree scope) |
| `quic.log` (6.1+), `tunnel.log`, `analyzer.log` | `server_name`, `client_initial_dcid`; `tunnel_type`; analyzer violations | QUIC/HTTP3 C2 and DoH over QUIC, encapsulation, protocol mismatches on standard ports |

## `conn_state` and `history`

| State | Meaning | | Letter | `history` meaning (upper = responder) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S0` | SYN seen, no reply: scan, blocked, or dead host | | `s` / `S` | SYN |
| `S1` | Established, never closed (still open or capture ended) | | `h` / `H` | SYN-ACK |
| `SF` | Normal establish and teardown | | `a` / `A` | ACK |
| `REJ` | SYN then RST: rejected | | `d` / `D` | payload data |
| `S2` / `S3` | Established, closed by one side only | | `f` / `F` | FIN |
| `RSTO` / `RSTR` | Reset by originator / responder after establishment | | `r` / `R` | RST |
| `RSTOS0` / `RSTRH` | Originator SYN then its RST; responder SYN-ACK then its RST | | `c` / `C` | bad checksum |
| `SH` / `SHR` | Half-open: SYN then FIN with no reply (`SHR` from responder) | | `t` / `T` | retransmission |
| `OTH` | No SYN seen; mid-stream (long-lived, asymmetric capture, capture started late) | | `g` / `G`, `w` / `W`, `i` / `I`, `q` / `Q`, `^` | content gap, zero window, inconsistent packet, multi-flag, direction flip |

`history` repeats a letter when the event recurs; `ShADadFf` is a clean exchange, `S` alone is a scan, `ShAD` with `S1` and a large `duration` is a session worth reading, and `^` means Zeek guessed the direction.

## TLS fingerprinting: JA3, JA3S, JA4

| Fingerprint | Built from | Use and limits |
|---|---|---|
| **JA3** (client) | TLS version, ciphers, extensions, curves, point formats, MD5 | Fast stacking of client software; brittle (extension order randomised by browsers since 2023, so one browser yields many JA3s) |
| **JA3S** (server) | Version, cipher, extensions of the ServerHello | Pair with JA3: a known C2 server answers a known client the same way every time |
| **JA4** (client) | `t13d1516h2_<cipher hash>_<extension hash>`: protocol, version, SNI present, cipher and extension counts, ALPN, then sorted hashes | Order-independent, human-readable prefix, far more stable than JA3; the FoxIO `zeek-ja4` package adds `ja4`, `ja4s`, `ja4h` (HTTP), `ja4x` (x509), `ja4t`/`ja4ts` (TCP), `ja4l` (latency) |
| **JA4S / JA4X** | Server hello; certificate issuer and subject RDN order | Server-side and certificate-side stacking; `ja4x` finds self-made certs that copy real subjects in the wrong order |
| **HASSH** | SSH KEX, ciphers, MACs, compression | Client/server SSH software fingerprint in `ssh.log` |

TLS 1.3 encrypts the certificate, so `ssl.log` has no `cert_chain_fps` or `x509.log` rows for most modern sessions: pivot on SNI, JA4, JA4S and `ssl_history` instead. **Encrypted Client Hello** hides the SNI too (rare in enterprises; an `ech` extension or an empty `server_name` to a CDN is itself a lead). Install fingerprinting with `zkg install zeek/salesforce/ja3`, `zkg install foxio/ja4` and `zkg install zeek/salesforce/hassh`; load `policy/protocols/conn/community-id-logging` and `policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files` in `local.zeek`.

## DNS anomaly checklist

- **Length and entropy**: queries over 50 characters, labels over 30, high Shannon entropy per label, many unique subdomains of one parent (tunnel or DGA); compute entropy in the SIEM, not in Zeek
- **Record types**: unusual volume of `TXT`, `NULL`, `CNAME`, `MX` or `ANY` from one client; `TXT` answers carrying base64
- **NXDOMAIN bursts**: high `rcode_name == NXDOMAIN` ratio per client (DGA); a sudden drop after a burst is a successful rendezvous
- **Resolver bypass**: UDP/TCP 53 to anything but your resolvers; TCP 53 from workstations; `dns.log` entries whose `id.resp_h` is external
- **DoH / DoT**: TCP 853 (DoT); TLS to known DoH endpoints (`dns.google`, `cloudflare-dns.com`, `dns.quad9.net`, `doh.opendns.com`) by SNI; QUIC on 443 to resolver IPs; a host with HTTPS traffic but almost no `dns.log` rows
- **Young and rare**: newly registered domains (under 30 days; enrich with a registration-date feed), rare TLDs for your estate (`.top`, `.xyz`, `.click`, `.icu` are overrepresented, lead only), punycode (`xn--`) look-alikes of your own brands
- **Answers**: low TTLs with many changing A records (fast flux), answers in RFC 1918 or loopback space for external names (rebinding, sinkholes), `0.0.0.0`
- **Services**: dynamic DNS and tunnel providers (`duckdns`, `no-ip`, `ngrok`, `trycloudflare`, `serveo`, `localtunnel`), paste and file-sharing domains from servers
- **Timing**: the same name queried at a fixed interval from one host, see the beacon section below

## Beacon and C2 detection methods

| Method | What to measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Interval regularity | Per (`id.orig_h`, `id.resp_h`, `id.resp_p`): sort by `ts`, take deltas, then count, mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation | Low CoV with many connections is a beacon; expect jitter of 10-50 %, so use percentiles or MAD rather than exact intervals |
| Jitter shape | Histogram of deltas: implants produce a tight band, humans produce a long tail | Cobalt Strike default `sleep 60` with `jitter 20` gives deltas in a 48-72 s band |
| Byte symmetry | `orig_bytes` and `resp_bytes` nearly constant per connection; tiny request, tiny response, hundreds of times a day | Also flag the opposite: one huge `orig_bytes` to a never-seen host (exfil) |
| Long sessions | `duration` over an hour, `conn_state` `S1`/`OTH` to external IPs | Reverse shells, persistent WebSockets, VPN-like tunnels |
| Rarity | Destinations contacted by one or two hosts in the estate, JA4s seen on one host, user agents seen once | Stack by day over 30 days; the long tail is the hunt |
| Protocol mismatch | `service` not matching `id.resp_p` (HTTP on 8443, SSH on 443, `-` on 443 with data) and `weird.log` names | Zeek's dynamic protocol detection does the work |
| Scoring tools | **RITA** (Active Countermeasures, Go rewrite) and **AC-Hunter** score beacons, long connections, DNS tunnelling and threat-intel hits from Zeek logs; **BZAR** maps `dce_rpc`/`smb` to ATT&CK lateral-movement techniques; **zeek-sniffpass** flags clear-text credentials | Point them at a day of logs first; they are fast |

## zeek-cut and jq one-liners

```bash
# Human-readable times, selected columns (TSV logs)
cat conn.log | zeek-cut -d ts id.orig_h id.resp_h id.resp_p service duration orig_bytes resp_bytes conn_state | head
# Top talkers by bytes out (candidate exfil)
cat conn.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h orig_bytes | awk '{b[$1" "$2]+=$3} END{for(k in b)print b[k],k}' | sort -rn | head
# Rare external destinations: pairs seen from only one source host
cat conn.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h local_resp | awk '$3=="F"' | sort -u | awk '{n[$2]++} END{for(d in n) if(n[d]==1) print d}' | head -50
# First-seen (orig, resp, port) pairs today versus a 30-day baseline file
cat conn.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h id.resp_p | sort -u > today.txt; comm -23 today.txt baseline_pairs.txt | head
# Long connections (> 1 hour) still open or mid-stream
cat conn.log | zeek-cut -d ts id.orig_h id.resp_h id.resp_p duration conn_state | awk '$5>3600' | sort -k5 -rn | head
# Beacon candidates: connection count and interval CoV per pair (needs at least 20 connections)
cat conn.log | zeek-cut ts id.orig_h id.resp_h id.resp_p | sort -k2,4 -k1n | awk '{k=$2" "$3" "$4; if(k==p){d=$1-t; n[k]++; s[k]+=d; ss[k]+=d*d} p=k; t=$1} END{for(k in n) if(n[k]>=20){m=s[k]/n[k]; v=ss[k]/n[k]-m*m; printf "%d %.1f %.2f %s\n", n[k], m, (v>0?sqrt(v)/m:0), k}}' | sort -k3n | head
# SMB share fan-out: one host mapping many admin shares
cat smb_mapping.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h path | grep -Ei 'admin\$|c\$' | sort -u | cut -f1 | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
# Kerberos: RC4 service-ticket requests (Kerberoasting signal) and pre-auth failures per client
cat kerberos.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h client service request_type cipher | awk '$4=="TGS" && $5 ~ /rc4/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
cat kerberos.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h error_msg | grep -i preauth | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
# NTLM from a host whose client name does not match its IP (relay or pass-the-hash lead)
cat ntlm.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h hostname username success | sort -u | head -40
# DNS: longest queries, NXDOMAIN storms, TXT-heavy clients
cat dns.log | zeek-cut query | awk '{print length($0), $0}' | sort -rn | head
cat dns.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h rcode_name | grep NXDOMAIN | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
cat dns.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h qtype_name | awk '$2=="TXT"' | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
# TLS: rare JA4s, self-signed or mismatched certs, SNI-less sessions
cat ssl.log | zeek-cut ja4 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n | head -30
cat ssl.log | zeek-cut server_name validation_status sni_matches_cert | grep -Ev 'ok\s+T' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
# JSON logs (LogAscii::use_json=T) with jq
jq -r 'select(.["id.resp_p"]==445) | [.["id.orig_h"], .["id.resp_h"], .conn_state] | @tsv' conn.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
jq -r 'select(.query|length>50) | [.["id.orig_h"], .query] | @tsv' dns.log | head
# Pivot a connection to its files and HTTP rows by uid
grep -F "$UID" files.log http.log ssl.log | zeek-cut -d ts uid id.resp_h
```

## Ports of interest (east-west)

| Port | Service | What abuse looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | SSH | Server-to-server pivoting, `-R`/`-D` tunnels, outbound SSH from servers that never used it |
| 88, 464 | Kerberos, kpasswd | RC4 TGS bursts (roasting), AS-REQ without pre-auth, password changes from odd hosts |
| 135, 49152-65535 | RPC endpoint mapper and dynamic ports | Remote WMI, service and task creation, DCOM; `dce_rpc.log` names the operation |
| 139, 445 | SMB | PsExec-style service installs, `ADMIN$`/`C$` writes, mass file writes (ransomware), share enumeration fan-out |
| 389, 636, 3268, 3269 | LDAP, LDAPS, Global Catalog | AD recon (`ldap_search.log` filters), LDAP relay, bulk queries from workstations |
| 3389 | RDP | Workstation-to-workstation RDP, new `client_name`s, NLA disabled, RDP tunnelled over SSH |
| 5985, 5986 | WinRM | PowerShell remoting from non-admin hosts |
| 1433, 1521, 3306, 5432, 27017, 6379 | Databases, Redis | Bulk reads, `xp_cmdshell`, unauthenticated Redis as a foothold |
| 53, 853, 443/udp | DNS, DoT, QUIC | Tunnelling, resolver bypass, DoH over QUIC |
| 80, 443, 8080, 8443 | HTTP(S) and proxies | C2 blends here; hunt by rarity, timing and fingerprint, not by port |
| 4444, 1337, 31337, 50050 | Default implant/listener ports | Lead only; mature C2 picks 443 |
| 21, 20, 69, 2049 | FTP, TFTP, NFS | Legacy exfil and staging; NFS mounts from unexpected clients |
| 161, 162, 514, 5601, 9200 | SNMP, syslog, Kibana, Elasticsearch | Recon of monitoring and log stores; log-destruction attempts |
| 2375, 2376, 6443, 10250 | Docker API, Kubernetes API, kubelet | Unauthenticated container runtime access; see the [Kubernetes playbook]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/playbooks/kubernetes-containers/) |

## PCAP quick triage

```bash
capinfos cap.pcap                                                       # duration, size, packet count
zeek -C -r cap.pcap local                                               # Zeek logs from a pcap (-C ignores checksums)
suricata -r cap.pcap -l out/                                            # IDS alerts into eve.json
tshark -r cap.pcap -q -z conv,tcp | sort -k10 -rn | head -30            # conversations by bytes
tshark -r cap.pcap -q -z endpoints,ip | head -30
tshark -r cap.pcap -Y 'http.request' -T fields -e ip.src -e http.host -e http.request.uri -e http.user_agent | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
tshark -r cap.pcap -Y 'dns.flags.response == 0' -T fields -e ip.src -e dns.qry.name -e dns.qry.type | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
tshark -r cap.pcap -Y 'tls.handshake.type == 1' -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
tshark -r cap.pcap -Y 'tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.flags.ack == 0' -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.dstport | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head   # SYN scans
tcpdump -nn -r cap.pcap 'port 445 and tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0' | head  # SMB connection attempts
tshark -r cap.pcap --export-objects http,objects/                        # carve HTTP downloads for hashing
```

## Ship Zeek to your SIEM

| Platform | Notes |
|---|---|
| Splunk | Splunk TA for Zeek (`sourcetype=zeek:conn:json`, `zeek:dns:json`, ...) or the Corelight App (`corelight_conn`); CIM mapping: `conn.log` to `Network_Traffic` (`src`, `dest`, `dest_port`, `bytes_in`/`bytes_out`, `transport`), `dns.log` to `Network_Resolution` (`query`, `reply_code`, `answer`), `http.log` to `Web` (`url`, `http_user_agent`, `status`), `ssl.log` to `Certificates`. Field names keep the dotted Zeek form (`id.orig_h`) |
| Microsoft Sentinel | Corelight data connector (`Corelight_v2_conn_CL` and siblings) or a custom log via the Azure Monitor Agent; ASIM `_Im_NetworkSession` and `_Im_Dns` parsers give a vendor-neutral schema (`SrcIpAddr`, `DstIpAddr`, `DstPortNumber`, `DnsQuery`) |
| Elastic | Filebeat `zeek` module to ECS (`source.ip`, `destination.ip`, `network.community_id`, `zeek.connection.state`), which joins cleanly with Suricata's module |
| Join keys | `uid` across Zeek logs, `fuid` to `files.log`, `community_id` across Zeek, Suricata, Corelight, AWS/Azure flow logs and EDR network events |

```spl
sourcetype=zeek:conn:json earliest=-24h local_orig=true local_resp=false
| eval src='id.orig_h', dest='id.resp_h', dport='id.resp_p'
| sort 0 src dest dport _time
| streamstats current=f last(_time) as prev by src dest dport
| eval delta=_time-prev
| stats count avg(delta) as avg_delta stdev(delta) as sd_delta sum(orig_bytes) as out_bytes by src dest dport
| where count>=20 AND avg_delta>10 AND sd_delta/avg_delta<0.3
| sort -count
```

```kql
Corelight_v2_conn_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and local_orig_b == true and local_resp_b == false
| sort by id_orig_h_s, id_resp_h_s, id_resp_p_d, TimeGenerated asc
| extend Delta = datetime_diff("second", TimeGenerated, prev(TimeGenerated)), SamePair = (id_orig_h_s == prev(id_orig_h_s) and id_resp_h_s == prev(id_resp_h_s) and id_resp_p_d == prev(id_resp_p_d))
| where SamePair
| summarize Count = count(), AvgDelta = avg(Delta), SdDelta = stdev(Delta), OutBytes = sum(orig_bytes_d) by id_orig_h_s, id_resp_h_s, id_resp_p_d
| where Count >= 20 and AvgDelta > 10 and SdDelta / AvgDelta < 0.3
| order by Count desc
```

Column names depend on the connector version; adapt them. Related: [C2 beaconing]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/playbooks/c2-beaconing/), [data exfiltration]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/playbooks/data-exfiltration/), [lateral movement]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/playbooks/lateral-movement/), the [query index]({{ site.baseurl }}/hunt/query-index/) and [practice datasets]({{ site.baseurl }}/labs/datasets/) with public Zeek logs.
